channel.name: 🏗️-die-sorter
channel.topic:
Discussion about the "wafer.space design sorter" that Andrew Wingate / evezor is designing to enable the service.

See more @ https://github.com/evezor/waferspace_die_sorter

messages.content:
*sorry, started replying and seems I got distracted*

haha, it's all useful, isn't it 😉 
At the base level, it's always nice to have *something* to look back on if there is some kind of issue somewhere. 
Additionally, Tim had wanted some kind of data on what shot in what wafer a die may have come from, it's difficult if something ever happens in the middle and you end up off by one or something, but it's in there anyways.

I ordered some more lights and stuff, I'll give it a shot. 
I haven't worked with ML models yet, but again, that's one of the reasons to just keep all the data so you may have a set to train against.
Thanks for the idea
Up camera is a fixed camera in a known location, we can move the robot above, knowing where the nozzle is, and correct pick errors. It's pretty common in a lot of pcb pnp machines.

Hey all, I was running the machine and was asked to post a little vid. I'll post more in the near future. I have a few I want to finish quickly, then do some small upgrades (better lighting and some small things)
Currently picking some @BreakingTaps dies. 
Basic setup is 
- robot arm
- cartesian bot below wafer that pushes die off tape
- other misc boards that power solenoids, or lights, or motors and a game controller
All the boards are networked over canbus

HUD is cpython bridged onto bus as well. All control is handled through a web interface (Starlette)
- up camera finds die on nozzle
- feeder_camera locates the pocket -- place happens between offsets from these
- down camera is on arm, does mostly calibration and location of the wafer (the dicing house sticks them on there all willy nilly, it's bad)

Like I said, more coming soon, feel free to ask questions
@Andrew Wingate are those run #2 wafers or testing on run #1 wafers?

Run #1 
Hoping to get Run #2 Wed hopefully, maybe, hopefully
Dicing house has them, they wanted to back grind again, so it's taking longer than we hoped.

Visualizing some of the pick data
Hopefully will be interesting to see improvements over time

I'm just going to dump these here.

My setup leaves a lot to be desired, sorry.

and the eyecandy still keeps coming!

I taped out these patterns that are just horizontal arrays of 1u wide metal strips, but with increasing spacing, to see if I could build a light wavelength filter. And you can see it sortof working.
In both the video and photos, the left handside of each pattern is some shade of red, shifting blue in hue towards the other end.
Ah, gorgeous!!
Not sure why video is not rendering for me, if others are having issues I will try to convert to h.264
One half of this block is metal strips in a consistent 1u spacing, and it consistently reflects mostly blue light, so I think this is working.

@Tholin more stills. 
Seems different things refract at different angles. But doesn't seem like discord is honoring the pic numbering. When I get to your die, I'll snatch one out and get some when I can hold it better by itself.
Yeah, that seems about right. The light direction most likely need to be aligned with the filter.
